minutes.headline: Assessors backed the senior tax-exemption option three, lowering the age and raising the reimbursement; they also set April 1 as next meeting.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors met with three members present. They heard from a resident about unanswered questions, got a status report on motor vehicle abatements, signed commitments, and discussed the certified five-year revaluation and the website. They voted to support option three for the 41C senior exemption and set April 1 as the next meeting, with April 22 and 29 tentative.

public_comment.topic: Thanked the board for putting assessment data online; asked for a date and process for answering residents' written questions, many of them simple, before the abatement request deadline.

Reimbursements come through the cherry sheet to the general fund, with limits on how many seniors are reimbursed.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted to support option three for the 41C senior exemption, which lowers the age and raises the reimbursement.
The board will tell the selectmen its support is behind option three, without retracting the earlier document.

Three members signed an annual software invoice, motor vehicle abatements, the last calendar-year 23 motor vehicle commitment and the fiscal 24 real estate and personal property commitment; the votes were not audible.
The board set April 1 as the next meeting, with April 22 tentative and April 29 as the fallback.
A resident asked for a date and process for answering written questions before the abatement request deadline; consolidating those questions goes on the next agenda.

why_it_matters: The 41C option the board backs sets the age and reimbursement terms for the senior property tax exemption, which affects who qualifies and how much of the cost falls on the town's overlay.
Residents with written questions for the assessors face a deadline for abatement requests, and the board has not yet set a date or process for answering them.
watch_next: Next Board of Assessors meeting on April 1, with April 22 and April 29 as tentative dates.
The next agenda is to take up consolidating the public questions and the ad hoc citizens committee on neighborhood definitions.

Most figure differences are caption damage. The thing to check is that our recording never caught the outcome of three votes, and the official minutes record "all in favor" on only two of them.
